en.name: Parsnips
en.summary: Parsnips are pale, sweet, carrot-shaped roots that get sweeter after a frost, because the plant converts starch to sugar. Refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below they keep 2–3 weeks from the day of purchase, and blanched and frozen they hold good quality for 10–12 months.
en.pantry: Parsnips are not a warm-room vegetable. They store well at cellar temperatures — traditionally left in the ground through winter — but in a heated or tropical kitchen they lose water quickly, go rubbery and turn from sweet to woody. There is no room-temperature figure here and none should be assumed. Refrigerate them as soon as you get home, unwashed and with any leafy tops cut off.
en.fridge: Store parsnips unwashed in a perforated bag or wrapped in kitchen paper in the crisper at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where they keep 2–3 weeks from purchase. Keep them dry but not desiccated: bare in the drawer they go limp in a week, sealed in plastic they sweat and grow mould at the tips. If they came with leafy tops, cut them off at once — the greens keep pulling moisture out of the root.
en.freezer: Parsnips must be blanched before freezing or their enzymes keep working and the flavour turns musty. Peel, cut into even batons or dice, boil for 2–3 minutes, plunge into iced water, drain thoroughly and pack airtight at −18 °C (0 °F). They are safe indefinitely and keep good quality for 10–12 months. Roasted parsnips also freeze well and reheat straight from frozen in a hot oven, which is often more useful than raw cubes.
en.thawing: Add frozen parsnips straight to soups, stews and roasting trays without thawing. If a recipe needs them thawed, thaw in the fridge and pat them dry, or they will steam instead of browning.
spoilage: Limp, bendy roots that no longer snap
Brown or black soft patches, especially at the tapered end
A woody, fibrous core that does not soften with cooking
Mould at the crown or tip, or a sour, musty smell
tips: Choose firm, pale, medium-sized roots; very large ones have a woody core.
Cut the leafy tops off the day you buy them.
Cut the woody core out of large parsnips before roasting.
Roast them rather than boiling them — the sugars caramelise and that is the whole point of a parsnip.

faq.q: How long do parsnips last in the fridge?
faq.a: 2–3 weeks from the day of purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, unwashed in a perforated bag in the crisper with the tops removed.
Yes, after blanching for 2–3 minutes. Packed airtight at −18 °C (0 °F) they keep good quality for 10–12 months. Roasted parsnips also freeze well.

faq.q: Why are parsnips sweeter in winter?
faq.a: Cold makes the plant convert stored starch into sugar as a kind of antifreeze. A parsnip lifted after a frost genuinely does taste sweeter.

faq.q: Do you have to peel parsnips?
faq.a: Small young ones can be scrubbed and left unpeeled. Larger roots are better peeled, and very large ones should have the woody central core cut out as well.

zh.name: 歐防風
zh.summary: 歐防風是外形像紅蘿蔔的淡色甜味根菜，經過霜期會變得更甜，因為植株會把澱粉轉成糖。4°C 以下冷藏，從購買當天算起可放 2～3 週；汆燙後冷凍則可維持 10～12 個月的良好品質。
zh.pantry: 歐防風不是能放在溫暖室內的蔬菜。它在地窖溫度下很耐貯——傳統上整個冬天就留在土裡——但在有暖氣或濕熱的廚房裡，它會很快失水、變得軟軟像橡皮，味道也從清甜轉成木質感。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。買回家請切掉葉子、不清洗直接冷藏。
zh.fridge: 不清洗，裝進打洞袋或用廚房紙巾包好，放在 4°C 以下的蔬果保鮮室，從購買日起可放 2～3 週。要保持乾爽但不能乾透：光溜溜放在抽屜裡一週就軟了，密封在塑膠袋裡則會悶出水、從尖端開始發霉。如果附有葉子，請立刻切掉——葉子會持續把水分從根部抽走。
zh.freezer: 歐防風一定要先汆燙再冷凍，否則酵素會繼續作用，味道會變得霉悶。去皮，切成大小一致的條或丁，滾水煮 2～3 分鐘，泡冰水冷卻，徹底瀝乾後密封放 −18°C。安全上可無限期保存，品質可維持 10～12 個月。烤好的歐防風也很耐冷凍，而且可以不解凍直接進高溫烤箱回熱，通常比生丁實用。
zh.thawing: 冷凍歐防風可以不解凍直接下湯、下燉鍋或進烤盤。食譜若需要解凍，請放冷藏室退冰並擦乾表面，否則下鍋只會冒水而不會上色。
spoilage: 出現褐色或黑色的軟爛斑塊，尤其是細尖的那一端
中心變成木質纖維，怎麼煮都不會軟
頭部或尖端長黴，或有酸味、霉味
tips: 挑結實、顏色淡、中等尺寸的；太大的中心多半已經木質化。
買回來當天就把葉子切掉。
大根的歐防風烤之前先把木質的中心挖掉。
用烤的而不是水煮——糖分焦糖化才是歐防風好吃的關鍵。

faq.q: 歐防風放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏，不清洗、去葉、裝打洞袋放蔬果室，從購買當天算起 2～3 週。
可以，先汆燙 2～3 分鐘。密封後放 −18°C，品質可維持 10～12 個月。烤好的也很適合冷凍。

faq.q: 歐防風為什麼冬天比較甜？
faq.a: 低溫會讓植株把儲存的澱粉轉成糖當作抗凍劑。經過霜期後採收的歐防風確實吃起來更甜。
小而嫩的刷洗乾淨後可以不削。比較大的建議削皮，而特別粗大的還要把中心的木質部分挖掉。
